# Cedarwood Studio

> A software studio that sells fixed-price engineering services to teams with an application in production. The services are a Rails Upgrade Roadmap and a Node.js Upgrade Roadmap, which show what a Rails or Node.js upgrade breaks before you commit to it ($2,500 each), and a CI Diagnostic, which shows why a GitHub Actions pipeline is slow or flaky and what to change first ($500). The measured pages below draw on public sample repositories that can be checked line by line. The upgrade reports are produced by a software factory with hundreds of upgrade rules drawn from official release notes and documentation, and a sandbox that runs the application's own test suite. Every report is carefully reviewed before it's delivered.

Cedarwood Studio is the business name of Jack Senechal, a sole proprietor. Contact: hello@cedarwood.studio. Prices are in US dollars and are fixed. Each page below carries the date it was last updated.

## Services

- [Rails Upgrade Roadmap, $2,500 fixed](https://cedarwood.studio/rails-upgrade-roadmap/): A fixed-price assessment of a Rails application's upgrade. The first version step is run in a sandbox, and the report says what breaks, with the file and line, including breaks the tests can't see. The deliverable is a reviewed report plus a staged plan with an effort range. Credited toward an upgrade started with the studio; the upgrade itself is quoted separately. Fits Rails apps on 7.0 or later, going to 8.1 or earlier, with a test suite that runs without production secrets and uses MariaDB, PostgreSQL and Redis at most. PostgreSQL works at the major version your CI, compose file or Dockerfile declares (11 to 18), with the standard extensions such as pgcrypto, uuid-ossp, citext, pg_trgm and hstore. A private gem source, a browser, suites that launch their own database from inside the tests and extensions beyond the standard set aren't covered; ask us first. Node.js applications have their own page, the Node.js Upgrade Roadmap, at https://cedarwood.studio/nodejs-upgrade-roadmap/. Delivered within 5 business days of payment and access. Last updated 2026-11-18.
- [Node.js Upgrade Roadmap, $2,500 fixed](https://cedarwood.studio/nodejs-upgrade-roadmap/): A fixed-price assessment of a Node.js application's upgrade. The first version step is run in a sandbox, and the report says what breaks, with the file and line, including breaks the tests can't see. The deliverable is a reviewed report plus a staged plan with an effort range. Credited toward an upgrade started with the studio; the upgrade itself is quoted separately. Fits Node.js applications on 16 or later, going to 26 or earlier, installed with npm, Yarn or pnpm, with a test suite on Mocha, Jest, Vitest, AVA or node:test that runs without production secrets and uses MariaDB, PostgreSQL and Redis at most. PostgreSQL fits when the tests reach it through a connection string or the standard PG environment variables. A private package registry, a browser, suites that start their own database containers (testcontainers) and extensions beyond the standard set aren't covered; ask us first. Framework, bundler or ORM upgrades such as Next.js, NestJS or Nuxt aren't covered either. Delivered within 5 business days of payment and access. Last updated 2026-11-18.
- [CI Diagnostic, $500 fixed](https://cedarwood.studio/github-actions-ci-diagnostic/): A fixed-price diagnostic of a slow or flaky GitHub Actions pipeline, measured from its own run history. A written report of where the time goes, which jobs fail and then pass on re-run, and the changes that give the most back, with the data behind each number. For GitHub Actions. Failing tests are named for pytest and unittest; with other test runners the report works at the level of jobs and steps. Delivered within 3 business days of payment and access. Last updated 2026-11-18.

## Measured answers

- [What breaks when upgrading Rails 7.1 to 8, and how long does each stage take?](https://cedarwood.studio/rails-7-1-to-8-upgrade-what-broke/): One measured upgrade of an open-source Rails application (Postal, about 27,000 lines, 851 test examples) from Rails 7.1.6 to 8.0.5.2: the nine lines flagged as breaking on the path to 8.1, what caught each one, what changed without breaking anything, the review rounds and fixes each stage took, and what a side-by-side browser comparison of 118 screen states showed. Last updated 2026-11-18.
- [How risky is a Rails upgrade, and how can you tell before you start?](https://cedarwood.studio/how-risky-is-a-rails-upgrade/): The story of one measured upgrade of an open-source Rails application (Postal, about 27,000 lines, 851 test examples) from Rails 7.1.6 to 8.0.5.2, told as a guide to judging an upgrade's risk before starting. On the unchanged code, the test suite ran 4 of the 16 lines in the application's code confirmed by reading to match a documented breaking change. One stage passed every test and every check and still didn't start with one optional feature on. Where the breaks were, what the stage reviews found, what a browser comparison showed, and five questions to ask of any upgrade. Last updated 2026-11-18.

## Public samples

- [cedarwood-studio/upgrade-roadmap-sample](https://github.com/cedarwood-studio/upgrade-roadmap-sample): one complete Upgrade Roadmap for Postal, an open-source Rails application (Rails 7.1 to 8.1), the record of the first four stages carried out on a fork, and a script that checks the report against its data. An unsolicited sample: nobody at the Postal project asked for it, and the studio is not affiliated with the project.
- [cedarwood-studio/ci-diagnostic-sample](https://github.com/cedarwood-studio/ci-diagnostic-sample): two complete CI Diagnostic reports on open-source projects (wagtail/wagtail and temporalio/sdk-python), with the data behind every number. Unsolicited samples, not affiliated with either project.
